title: Adobe After Effects Advanced Core v1

domain.name: Adobe After Effects Advanced
domain.description: Advanced compositing, motion design, expressions, tracking, keying, 3D layers, render optimization, and reusable template workflows in After Effects.

competencies.name: Compositing Order & Precomp Architecture
competencies.description: Structure composites so transforms, mattes, effects, and precomps behave predictably.
competencies.purpose: Build scenes that remain editable instead of collapsing under layer complexity.

units.title: Order of operations changes the result
units.content: Masking, effects, transforms, collapse transformations, blending, and precompositions can change how pixels are generated; understand the stage at which each operation happens.

units.title: Composite architecture workflow
units.content: Separate source prep, element composites, scene composites, and delivery comps; precompose for a clear reason; name control layers; preserve source layers; test edge cases before duplicating structures.

units.title: Compositing architecture failures
units.content: Avoid precomps with unclear purpose, duplicate effects spread across many layers, hidden transform assumptions, and destructive rasterization of elements that still need adjustment.

drills.title: Debug a broken precomp chain
drills.prompt: Given unexpected scale, blur, and matte behavior across nested precomps, map the likely operation-order issue.

competencies.name: Keying, Rotoscoping & Edge Integration
competencies.description: Separate subjects cleanly and integrate edges into the target background.
competencies.purpose: Create believable composites from imperfect production footage.

units.title: Keying and roto workflow
units.content: Evaluate source quality; choose key, roto, or hybrid; create a stable core matte; refine edges separately; suppress spill carefully; restore believable motion blur, grain, and light interaction.

units.title: A perfect matte can still look fake
units.content: Integration requires edge softness, color contamination, grain, defocus, motion blur, and scene lighting to agree with the destination shot.

units.title: Keying failures
units.content: Avoid choking every edge equally, over-denoising before keying, destroying fine detail to remove spill, and judging the matte only on black.

drills.title: Composite a difficult greenscreen subject
drills.prompt: Plan a workflow for hair detail, uneven screen, spill, and a darker replacement background.

competencies.name: Tracking, Stabilization & Match Move
competencies.description: Track motion for inserts, stabilization, screen replacement, and scene attachment.
competencies.purpose: Attach graphics or fixes convincingly to moving footage.

units.title: Tracking workflow
units.content: Define the motion you need to solve; choose point, planar, camera, or manual tracking accordingly; track high-information regions; inspect drift; correct or retrack weak segments; apply through a controllable intermediary such as a null when useful.

units.title: Track the motion model, not the object label
units.content: A flat sign needs planar behavior; a camera move through space may need 3D camera solve; choosing by visual subject name rather than motion geometry causes weak tracks.

units.title: Tracking failures
units.content: Avoid tracking low-detail regions, accepting small drift that compounds, stabilizing before deciding the desired final framing, and baking track data directly into many layers without control.

drills.title: Plan a phone-screen replacement
drills.prompt: Choose a tracking method and integration steps for a perspective-changing handheld phone.

competencies.name: Expressions & Motion Control Systems
competencies.description: Use expressions and controllers to automate relationships without making rigs opaque.
competencies.purpose: Build scalable motion systems and editable templates.

units.title: Expressions encode relationships
units.content: Use expressions for dependencies, constraints, procedural timing, and repeated logic; avoid replacing simple keyframes with code just because code is possible.

units.title: Expression rig workflow
units.content: Define the behavior and editable inputs; expose controls; reference layers by stable naming or effects; clamp or validate ranges; add fallbacks where practical; test duplicated and reordered layers.

units.title: Expression failures
units.content: Avoid hidden dependencies, circular references, index-only logic that breaks on reorder, uncontrolled random values, and expressions no one can safely edit or disable.

drills.title: Build a responsive title rig
drills.prompt: Design controls for text length, padding, background size, and entry/exit timing.

competencies.name: Motion Design Timing & Graph Control
competencies.description: Shape animation with timing, spacing, easing, overshoot, and hierarchy.
competencies.purpose: Create motion that feels intentional rather than mechanically interpolated.

units.title: The graph is the motion
units.content: Keyframe positions do not describe how fast motion travels between them; speed/value curves determine weight, emphasis, and rhythm.

units.title: Motion polish workflow
units.content: Block poses and timing; fix hierarchy of entrances; shape acceleration/deceleration; add overlap only after primary motion works; review at speed; remove motion that competes with the message.

units.title: Motion design failures
units.content: Avoid identical easing on every property, random overshoot, decorative motion on every element, and polishing curves before the sequence timing reads.

drills.title: Refine a logo reveal
drills.prompt: Plan the timing hierarchy and graph behavior for a restrained premium logo reveal.

competencies.name: 3D Layers, Cameras & Lighting
competencies.description: Use After Effects 3D space, cameras, lights, and depth cues for motion graphics and compositing.
competencies.purpose: Create spatial motion while understanding AE's layer-based 3D limits.

units.title: AE 3D is compositing-oriented
units.content: Layer 3D, camera projection, and lights can create strong spatial scenes, but geometry and physically complex interactions may belong in a dedicated 3D application.

units.title: 3D comp workflow
units.content: Set comp/camera assumptions; organize 3D layers around meaningful nulls; establish depth and parallax; control camera movement; add light/shadow only when it serves the shot; pre-render expensive external 3D when appropriate.

units.title: AE 3D failures
units.content: Avoid extreme camera moves that expose flat layers, inconsistent scale/depth, unnecessary lights, and forcing a heavy 3D problem into AE when Blender or an engine is better.

drills.title: Build a 3D parallax promo scene
drills.prompt: Plan camera, layer depth, focal hierarchy, and handoff for a layered promotional shot.

competencies.name: Effects, Color & Grain Integration
competencies.description: Match inserted elements using blur, color, noise, distortion, glow, and grain.
competencies.purpose: Make composites feel captured together rather than merely layered together.

units.title: Integration pass
units.content: Match scale and perspective first; match exposure and color; match sharpness/defocus and motion blur; reproduce lens or atmospheric behavior where needed; add grain/noise last at the appropriate stage.

units.title: Match defects, not just ideal color
units.content: Real footage contains noise, softness, lens distortion, bloom, rolling shutter, and compression; composited elements often look fake because they are too perfect.

units.title: Integration failures
units.content: Avoid using glow as universal realism, adding grain before resizing, overmatching black levels until detail disappears, and compensating for bad perspective with color effects.

drills.title: Integrate a CG sign into footage
drills.prompt: Plan the final effects stack for a rendered sign placed into handheld night footage.

competencies.name: Render Performance & Reusable Templates
competencies.description: Manage cache, pre-renders, proxies, render queues, and template design for repeatable output.
competencies.purpose: Keep complex AE projects responsive and production-ready.

units.title: Performance workflow
units.content: Identify the expensive layer/effect; isolate bottlenecks; pre-render stable branches; use proxies for heavy sources; manage cache intentionally; preserve source comps; render a tested master before derivatives.

units.title: Pre-render stable complexity
units.content: If a branch is expensive but unlikely to change, render it to reduce repeated calculation while retaining the editable source comp.

units.title: Performance failures
units.content: Avoid deleting source comps after pre-render, relying on cache as archive, rendering every experiment as a new untracked file, and packaging templates with missing dependencies.

drills.title: Prepare an AE template handoff
drills.prompt: Create a handoff plan for a branded opener with editable text, media replacements, and protected animation.
